ar3.justification: Legitimately internal: an instrument that measures the seam creates none, and ARBITRATION §3 expressly allows this provided it is reported. It is reported here, and the irony is load-bearing rather than decorative - the piece that owns the project's seam-crossing floor demonstrated zero crossings, and its own scanner reported four real, data-backed crossings as absent, one of which was built specifically to answer a previous seam_sterile verdict.

consumption.ruling: ACCEPTED for this piece, decided rather than applied mechanically. RI-MTH07 exists for a specific harm - a WORLD model the running world never reads, so that from the player's chair a correct model and a missing one are the same thing. Instrument data has no player-facing surface to be dead in. Both artifacts are generated from corpus items and consumed by tools, and both consumptions are demonstrated by perturbation: cells-from-md --self-test mutates a copy of the item four ways and requires the generator to go red (4/4), probes-from-md likewise (4/4). Scoring these 0 would assert the instrument does not work, which is false, and the builder declared the situation rather than papering over it.
consumption.transferred_failure: The rule's SPIRIT transfers exactly and it fails. For an instrument piece the prior question is 'is any of it plugged in?'. Every importer of tools/experience/lib/sabotage.mjs across tools/ and game/ is W1-25's own: matrix-probe.mjs, breakage-probe.mjs, anecdote-verify.mjs, sabotage.mjs, sabotage-cases.mjs. Zero adopters outside the piece. matrix-probe.mjs has never touched a browser; breakage-probe.mjs performs no breakage. A general facility with no caller outside the piece that wrote it is a library, not an instrument - the same failure the piece exists to name, one level up.

score.band_label: The best instrument in this corpus, pointed at nothing. Four items, four hard fails, no crossing demonstrated, no anecdote measured, no breakage performed. 2.0 is the minimum over RI-CMP01 (2), RI-EXP02 (2), RI-EXP03 (2) and RI-EXP06 (2), each capped by its own hard fails. The band understates the craft and states the outcome correctly: what exists is scaffolding of unusually high quality with nothing yet standing on it.

biggest_gap.what: The sabotage facility fails when its arms agree, and whether it can SEE that they agree is delegated to `support` - a caller-supplied field that is optional, undefined by default, unvalidated, and whose two honest readings give opposite verdicts on the strongest real inert control on this tree. W1-14-r3's shipped `--break=nocast`, which a human critic ruled inert, comes back OK when support is 'effects examined' (55/55), VACUOUS when it is 'effects delivered' (55/0), and OK again when the caller omits support entirely. Four further holes in the same cascade: two arms whose value is `undefined` canonicalise to agreement and return INERT (a confident claim about a measurement that never happened - I hit this by accident on my first run, against a real artifact); MASKED is last in the cascade and is shadowed by any unmet margin or wrong direction; armsAgree is decided on intact-vs-all-broken alone, so a control with a demonstrably live factor is reported INERT under cancellation while the same record lists that factor as moving it; and the documented obligation on the `supportArms:'intact'` escape hatch (a caller 'must say why, in support_note') is enforced nowhere and support_note is not even copied onto the result, so the canonical W1-13 failure passes with a one-key spec change.
biggest_gap.why_it_matters: This piece exists to make the project's most common failure detectable, and PLAYTHROUGH-CRITIC §10 names 'the control is never run' as the most likely failure in the corpus. Every one of the five holes above is that same failure occurring inside the facility built to catch it. Worse for adoption: the facility is meant to be used by other pieces, and the first thing a new caller writes is measure(). Two of the three ways a careful engineer would fill in `support` cause the facility to pass an inert control, and the third - omitting it - is the default.

remedy.action: Four changes, all in tools/experience/lib/sabotage.mjs. (1) MAKE SUPPORT MANDATORY: runControl already throws on a spec with no factors ('a control with no factors is not a control'); throw the same way when any arm returns no finite support - a control that cannot say what it ranged over is not a control. Amend the docstring's 'the number of units the measurement ranged over' to 'units that REACHED THE COMPARATOR', which is the single word separating A1 from A2. (2) ADD `NO_MEASUREMENT`: when every arm's value canonicalises to 'null', say that instead of INERT - the same argument the file already makes for VACUOUS. (3) ADD `SHORT_CIRCUIT` for the fourth failure shape, fired when the broken arm's support collapses relative to the intact arm's; both numbers are already on every arm record. (4) FIX THE CASCADE: hoist `masked` above the margin and direction tests, make armsAgree read `distinct_values === 1` (computed one line above), and throw when supportArms:'intact' arrives with no support_note, carrying that note onto the result so a report can list every control that opted out.
remedy.acceptance: Re-run `node tools/experience/critic-w1-25.mjs --a --b` against the amended facility. A1 and A3 must become ERROR or NO_MEASUREMENT rather than OK; A4 must become NO_MEASUREMENT; B-COLLIDE-1 must become MASKED; B-COLLIDE-2 must stop being INERT; B-COLLIDE-4 must throw. `--self-test` 6/6, the three existing facility breaks and `--cases` 8/8 must all still pass, and a FOURTH facility break `--break=support-optional` must be added and shown going red. The acceptance harness is already on the tree and does not need writing.

ARBITRATION §3's CONSUMPTION clause is written for world models. Does an instrument piece discharge it by demonstrating tool-side consumption under perturbation (as W1-25 did), or does the clause simply not apply? This verdict rules the former and adds a transferred test - does anything outside the piece import the facility - which W1-25 fails. That transferred test is not in the doctrine and probably should be.

notes: This is the fairest FAIL I know how to write. The builder shipped the single most rigorous instrument in this corpus - a general facility that fails when its arms agree, replays three real historical inert controls from the artifacts that produced them, goes red when broken three ways on purpose, and reports its own voided run, its own three false positives and its own unbuilt tools without being asked. It also shipped a headline crossing number that is wrong, an overstated claim about the traces, and a facility whose own control against the project's most common failure is an optional field. Both halves are true and the score reflects the second because that is what the items measure. Nothing here should be read as a reason to build the next instrument less carefully; it is a reason to run this one. SOURCE READS (CRITIC-DOCTRINE §1.1, labelled here as required): every source read in this verdict is either `diagnose-after-demonstrating` — the cascade in lib/sabotage.mjs and the pattern table in matrix-scan.mjs were read only AFTER the behaviour was demonstrated from output by tools/experience/critic-w1-25.mjs, and events.js only after the zero-event trace was counted — or `quote-written-content`, for the four data fields in game/data/world/encounters.json which ARE the artifact, or `locate-harness` for sabotage-cases.mjs. No score in this verdict rests on a source-code claim without a corresponding output artifact.
